estimand: Equal case, equal try within case; minutes summed and unsafe averaged over frozen maintenance checkpoints.

pooled_comparison_only.warning: Unpaired and unclustered; different pooled weights with unequal tries/steps; never a fallback.

variance.method: Equal-case within covariance; sample covariance of case means minus mean(S_i/n_i). Negative eigenvalues projected to zero; raw estimates retained. Case-only percentile bootstrap.
variance.zero_minute_transform: log(1 + total charged minutes); includes genuine zeros, no dropped tries.
variance.within_interpretation: Includes stochastic checkpoint outcomes, not a separately identified latent agent propensity.

next_round_sizing.rule: After all frozen measurement cases are scored, fit equal-case random-effects covariances to log(1 + charged minutes) and unsafe checkpoint fractions per try. Use the measured-component generator in steadiness.py, retaining case, try and paired covariance, under a fixed planning alternative of 50% time saving and zero safety difference, at the measured baseline mean minutes. For 2 and 3 tries separately, scan the frozen case grid [24,36,48,72,96,128,192,256,384,512]. Use 2500 simulated studies and 999 paired case-then-try bootstrap draws per study, seed 20261017; apply fixed-sample rule C (one-sided 95%, saving >30%, safety <=+5 points, collapsed-safety guard). Select the first grid size whose Wilson 95% Monte Carlo LOWER power bound is at least 80%; stop that design's simulation scan there and report every tested grid point. Check moment reproduction and simulate each null boundary at the candidate size; withhold a recommendation if moments differ materially, any boundary rejection LOWER Monte Carlo bound exceeds 5%, safety is collapsed, or baseline minutes are zero. If none qualifies, report beyond 512/undetermined, never extrapolate. This sizes a future separately frozen round, never adds tries or cases to this measurement round, and is conditional on estimated components and the Gaussian summary model; it does not include component-estimation uncertainty.
next_round_sizing.assumptions: Gaussian case/try summary effects with measured cross-covariances; bounded rate difference, censored shifted-lognormal minutes. Does not simulate discrete checkpoints, or unidentified failures. Component uncertainty excluded.

third_try_subset_rule: Freeze case IDs, maintenance steps, paired try IDs and the third-try subset before any scores are seen; choose the subset independently of outcomes (prefer a seeded random subset balanced by writer family). Average checkpoints within try for safety; sum minutes within try; average tries within case, then cases equally. Resample paired cases and then paired tries, retaining each selected case's original try count and all checkpoints. Third-try cases get no extra case weight. A fixed subset is unbiased for mean minutes/rates conditional on these cases if tries are exchangeable and subset membership is outcome-independent. The saving ratio and kappa have ordinary finite-sample nonlinear bias; no exact unbiasedness is claimed for them. Missing planned tries are an error, not a new subset.

subset_simulation.note: Checkpoint rate and minute means are unbiased; the ratio saving need not be exactly unbiased.

limitations: Percentile cluster bootstrap coverage is approximate with 24 cases, especially rare failures.
Collapsed safety cannot certify non-inferiority: an empirical bootstrap cannot invent unseen failures.
Kappa depends on prevalence; undefined when every label is identical. Read plain disagreement first.
Variance estimates are noisy at 2–3 tries, assume exchangeable tries, and truncate negative component eigenvalues.
A 95% interval is uncertainty under this case-generating design, not a guarantee for production.
Freeze design, subset, scoring and script hashes before scoring; run once after completion. The script cannot verify when a file was frozen.

plan.bayesian_likelihood: Joint Gaussian paired try summaries (B minutes/100, C minutes/100, C-B unsafe fraction), case and try covariance; bounded population effects, not bounded Gaussian observations
plan.bayesian_covariance_prior: Independent inverse-Wishart G,W: df=5, scale=diag(.25,.25,.01); prior mean component SD scales 50 minutes, 50 minutes, 10 safety points; heavy tails; same for every effect prior
plan.bayesian_baseline_prior: log(B population mean minutes/100) Normal(0,2.5); saving <1; safety difference in [-1,1]
plan.calibration_generator: steadiness.generate_batch: binary checkpoints and discrete charges, base unsafe .15, base minutes 30/checkpoint, level 0; same 24-case unequal-try design as fixture
plan.calibration_note: Shorter chains for computational calibration; record diagnostics and threshold Monte Carlo ambiguity. Model-conditional error rate, not a universal frequentist guarantee.
plan.mixed_sizing_agreement: Both fits must converge without singularity or quadrature sensitivity; each model marginal and paired variance within 25% of reference (absolute tolerance 1e-5). Reference cross-outcome covariance retained and resulting covariance projected PSD only if relative change <=10%. Reference sizes remain primary; model feeds a power sensitivity at the reference candidate sizes.

sceptical.warning: Gaussian try-summary approximation; may assign impossible observation values. This is a joint hierarchical posterior with full covariance uncertainty; not a logistic Bayesian GLMM or a rule-C decision.

no_difference.note: No-difference safety non-inferiority is true, so its threshold crossing alone is not a false finding. All studies, including poor diagnostics, remain in the denominator; this is algorithm calibration.

bayesian.interpretation: A posterior around 70% is weak evidence, not a finding. Posterior probabilities never change rule C; priors and Gaussian working-likelihood assumptions matter.

log_minutes.method: Gaussian REML on log(1+charged minutes); try covariance is within-case residual covariance
log_minutes.optimizer_message: CONVERGENCE: RELATIVE REDUCTION OF F <= FACTR*EPSMCH
log_minutes.interval_method: case-bootstrap refitting, no Wald intervals; conditional on successful fits

unsafe_glmm.method: Binomial logistic GLMM; paired bivariate case and try-within-case random effects; Gaussian-Hermite integration
unsafe_glmm.optimizer_message: CONVERGENCE: RELATIVE REDUCTION OF F <= FACTR*EPSMCH
unsafe_glmm.coefficient_scale: conditional C-B log odds, not a risk difference
unsafe_glmm.interval_method: case-bootstrap refitting, no Wald intervals; conditional on successful fits

sizing_input.unsafe_conversion: Marginal probability-scale case covariance plus try propensity covariance and binomial checkpoint noise. Assumes conditionally independent checkpoint Bernoullis; not latent logit variances plugged into a rate generator.
sizing_input.cross_outcome_covariance: Unidentified by separate models; use bootstrap reference cross-covariances when comparing a model sensitivity input.

mixed_effects.sizing_policy: Bootstrap variance components remain the reference. Mixed-model components are an explicitly secondary sensitivity input, never an override.

sizing_sensitivity.reference: bootstrap components always retain the primary sizing result
sizing_sensitivity.status: bootstrap reference retained: model singular/unstable or variance disagreement

covariate_adjustment.method: Four pre-fixed case folds; slopes trained without held-out cases; case-bootstrap refits preserve fold membership for duplicate selections. Inference conditions on the frozen case-set covariate mean, not an unknown population mean.

validation_assembly.note: Primary, posterior/model fits and binary-checkpoint calibration computed as separate full validations on the same synthetic fixture; no real results. Assembly verifies scored-file hashes and measured covariance components. The added calibration replaces the earlier Gaussian working-model calibration.
